- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.3) — model tends to overshoot, especially after spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.1) — model is overly conservative, fails to capture early reversal or momentum.
- Lag in price response: model often lags true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in trending markets.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp moves, leading to false peaks or troughs in forecast.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate by 1–3% in high sentiment, underperform in low sentiment.
- Avoid “sudden spike” extrapolation — model tends to project continued momentum after short-term spikes, ignoring volatility decay.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.4, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to account for overconfidence; if sentiment < 0.2, increase by 0.5–1.5% to capture underreaction.
